facts.fact: The NITA-U National Information Security Policy 2026 states that the Uganda National Cybersecurity Strategy (2022-2026), developed by the Government through the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance, is in place and that the policy translates its objectives into mandatory requirements.

The document defines CERT-UG as Uganda's national computer emergency response team, operated under NITA-U, providing incident coordination, vulnerability advisories and threat intelligence, and states it functions as the national CSIRT; the document gives no date of creation, so its publication date is used.

The policy, stated to be mandatory for operators of critical information infrastructure, requires MDAs, local governments and critical infrastructure operators to report information security breaches to the National CSIRT/CERT-UG; this is a national policy requirement, and the document lists no designated CII operators.

systems.tiers: national, listed as a strategy initiative to establish

note: No incident handled, alert issued or published count is stated; the NCCC is only an initiative to establish.
